{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Irena Peeva 1995 (portion B).jpg|thumb|upright|Peeva in 1995]]
'''Irena Vassileva Peeva''' is a professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Cornell University]], specializing in [[commutative algebra]].<ref>[https://math.cornell.edu/irena-peeva Faculty profile], Cornell University, retrieved 2018-10-30.</ref> She disproved the [[Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture]] jointly with [[Jason McCullough]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = McCullough | first1 = Jason
 | last2 = Peeva | first2 = Irena
 | doi = 10.1090/jams/891
 | issue = 2
 | journal = Journal of the American Mathematical Society
 | mr = 3758150
 | pages = 473–496
 | title = Counterexamples to the Eisenbud–Goto regularity conjecture
 | url = http://orion.math.iastate.edu/jmccullo/papers/Regularity.pdf
 | volume = 31
 | year = 2018| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Peeva did her graduate studies at [[Brandeis University]], earning a Ph.D. in 1995 under the supervision of [[David Eisenbud]] with a thesis entitled ''Free Resolutions''.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=22655}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and a [[C. L. E. Moore instructor]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]
before joining the Cornell Department of Mathematics faculty in 1998.<ref>[https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~irena/papers/cv.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2018-10-30.</ref>

Peeva is an editor of the Transactions of AMS.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~irena/papers/bio.pdf|title=Bio|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

==Books==
Peeva is the author of:
* ''Graded Syzygies'' (Springer, 2011).<ref>Reviews of ''Graded Syzygies'': Christopher A. Francisco (2011), {{MR|2560561}}; Peter Schenzel, {{zbl|1213.13002}}</ref>
* ''Minimal Free Resolutions over Complete Intersections'' (with [[David Eisenbud]], Springer, 2016).<ref>Reviews of ''Minimal Free Resolutions over Complete Intersections'': Benjamin P. Richert, {{MR|3445368}}; Michael Brown, {{zbl|1342.13001}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2014 Peeva was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to commutative algebra and its applications."<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows 2014 Class of the Fellows of the AMS], retrieved 2014-06-16.</ref>

In 2019/2020 and in 2012/2013 Peeva was a Simons Foundation fellow.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics|date=2012-06-19|website=Simons Foundation|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref> During 1999-2001 she was a Sloan Foundation fellow<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows|title=Past Fellows|website=sloan.org|access-date=2019-10-06|archive-date=2018-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was a Sloan doctoral dissertation fellow in 1994/1995.
